_readme: Machine identity and the lease authority for the two-robot installation. `slots` maps the two logical slots (alpha, beta — the values the floor and cjap_is use) to real hostnames; a machine finds its own slot by hostname (override: CJ_ROBOT_SLOT). Hostnames identify MACHINES only — the persona (Panganiban vs Host) is `cjap_is`, held by the authority and assignable from the console. `authority` is where the console/lease server runs (one machine); the other machine's dashboard proxies /console there and its robot polls it. Relocating the authority = change `authority.host`, sync, restart pi-dashboard on both. Robots never talk to each other. 2026-09-12: the second machine is `reachy2` (192.168.88.10) and keeps that name — `slots.beta` follows the machine, the machine is not renamed to suit the config. `authority.ip` (2026-09-12) is optional and, when set, replaces the `{host}.local` URL everywhere: mDNS is the fragile part of the link (guest networks block it), so on the venue kit give the authority a DHCP reservation on the travel router and put that address here. `host` still names the MACHINE — it is what each robot compares its hostname against to know whether it IS the authority, so never put an address in it.

sync_remote._note: bare repo for offline git sync between the two machines (no internet needed); ~/git/cjap.git on the authority machine today, add the other machine with `git remote add <name> pollen@<host>.local:git/cjap.git` when it is reachable
